title: Skill Hub Run Trace Event
description: One user-visible Run Trace event (TRACE-001). This is the Run Trace plane of ADR-009 only: platform observability and evaluation results use different models and are NOT carried here. Every instance is one row of the `trace_events` partitioned table (db/migrations/0004).

schema_version.description: Trace event contract version. Minor bumps are additive only; a breaking change bumps the major and gets a new $id. 1.1 added usagePayload.token_source; a producer writing only 1.0 fields may keep declaring 1.0, and a 1.0 event is a valid 1.1 event.

event_id.description: Producer-assigned UUID. This is the consumer idempotency key: delivery is at-least-once, so a consumer that has already stored this event_id must treat a redelivery as a no-op.

run_id.description: Permanent platform run identifier (ADR-004, iron rule 10). Never a provider_run_id.

attempt.description: Platform run attempt this event belongs to (ADR-004 run_attempt). Mirrors runs.attempt.

seq.description: Gapless monotonic ordinal, starting at 1, scoped to the (run_id, attempt, emitted_by) stream. A hole in a producer's sequence is how a lost event is detected (TRACE-001, TRACE-008). Cross-producer ordering is (occurred_at, emitted_by, seq), never seq alone.
seq.$comment: Scoped per producer, not per run: no single writer can hand out a run-wide counter without becoming a serialization point, and a run-wide counter assigned at ingest time would make loss undetectable by construction.

occurred_at.description: Producer clock, RFC 3339 with offset. Clocks across producers may skew; seq is authoritative within a stream, occurred_at only merges streams.

emitted_by.description: Producing plane. `sandbox` events cross the trust boundary (ADR-001) and are untrusted input to the control plane.

status.description: Coarse outcome for list views and filtering (TRACE-001 requires a status). Detail lives in the payload.

masked.description: True when the masker (TRACE-005) has run over this event. Events with masked=false MUST NOT be persisted or displayed (iron rule 11, NFR-002).

masked_fields.description: JSON Pointers, relative to `payload`, of values actually replaced by the redaction placeholder. Empty means the masker ran and found nothing.

payload_object_key.description: Object storage key holding the full payload when it exceeded the inline size budget. When set, `payload` holds the truncated form and the relevant `truncated` flag is true.

runStatus.$comment: Mirrors the run_status enum in db/migrations/0004. Kept in lockstep by hand; the DB enum is the definition.

skillActivationPayload.description: TRACE-002. The agent decided to use, or not use, a skill that was made available to the run.

resourceReadPayload.description: TRACE-002. A file inside the skill package (or a mounted dataset) was read by the workload.

resource_path.description: Path relative to the package or dataset mount root. Absolute sandbox paths are not exported.

toolCallPayload.description: TRACE-003. One completed tool invocation, emitted once on completion and carrying its own duration.
toolCallPayload.$comment: Single event rather than a start/end pair: a pair doubles the row count in a partitioned table, forces the UI to self-join to show a duration, and leaves a dangling start whenever the sandbox dies mid-call. Latency (TRACE-004) is satisfied by duration_ms. If the general-mode progress view (TRACE-006) later needs an in-flight indicator, add a `tool_call_started` type additively - do not retrofit a phase field here.

invocation_id.description: Agent-side call id, for correlating a tool_call with the agent_output that consumed it.

arguments.$comment: sensitivity: secret_bearing - caller-controlled, routinely carries credentials and dataset contents.

result_summary.$comment: sensitivity: secret_bearing - tool output, untrusted and possibly secret-carrying.

mcpCallPayload.description: PLACEHOLDER. Remote MCP is out of the MVP first release (see AGENTS.md scope note), so only the type is reserved here to keep event_type stable when MCP lands. Payload shape is deliberately unconstrained and MUST NOT be relied on until it is specified; the masking and ordering rules of this contract still apply.
mcpCallPayload.$comment: sensitivity: secret_bearing (whole object) - MCP arguments and results carry server credentials. Specify the shape in the batch that implements MCP collection (TRACE-003).

scriptLogPayload.description: TRACE-003. One chunk of script output from inside the sandbox.

message.description: Text after masking. Consumers must render this as inert text: no ANSI, HTML, SVG or executable interpretation (ADR-009).

truncated.description: True when this chunk was cut. The full text, if retained, is at the envelope's payload_object_key.

dropped_bytes.description: Bytes removed by truncation or by a per-run log budget. Null means unknown, which the UI must show as unknown rather than zero.

agentOutputPayload.description: TRACE-004. Agent-produced text. The final answer of a run is kind=final.

text.$comment: sensitivity: secret_bearing - model output over user prompts and datasets; also untrusted content (prompt injection), render inert.

errorPayload.description: TRACE-004. A failure worth showing the user. Category follows the ADR-004 failure taxonomy so retry policy and diagnostics line up with the orchestrator.

category.$comment: ADR-004 'failure and retry': provision / execution / event delivery / artifact upload / evaluation / cleanup are classified separately.

code.description: Stable diagnostic code (NFR-003). Not a provider code; provider detail goes in provider_diagnostics.

message.$comment: sensitivity: secret_bearing - error text frequently embeds URLs, tokens and argument values.

retryable.description: Whether the orchestrator considered this action safe to retry (ADR-004: only known-idempotent, policy-allowed actions). Recording the decision, not making it.

provider_diagnostics.description: Provider-specific extension fields (ADR-004). May be stored and shown, but evaluation must not depend on them.
provider_diagnostics.$comment: sensitivity: secret_bearing - provider payloads are not vetted field by field.

usagePayload.description:
TRACE-004. Token and cost accounting for one model call or one run-level rollup. All model traffic goes through the LiteLLM gateway (iron rule 8), so these numbers come from the gateway response, never from a provider SDK.

A run-total rollup is emitted once per run whether or not the agent turn reached a clean end - see token_source. An absent usage event means the producer never got to report at all, and a consumer must render that as unreported, never as zero (EVAL-012 sums these and would otherwise undercount every abnormal run).

cache_read_input_tokens.description: Cached input tokens billed at the reduced rate. NULL means the gateway did not report the field - which is the current state on LiteLLM's /v1/messages route.
cache_read_input_tokens.$comment: Known gap, not a bug in this contract: pdm-003-litellm-spike-report section 11.5.2 measured LiteLLM 1.96.2 omitting cache_read_input_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens entirely on /v1/messages (absent, not zero), while /v1/chat/completions reports them correctly. Budgeting is unaffected; observability is. Consumers MUST render null as 'unreported', never as 0.

cache_write_input_tokens.description: Input tokens written into the prompt cache. NULL has the same 'unreported' meaning as cache_read_input_tokens.

cost_usd.description: Cost as reported by the gateway. NULL when unavailable; the UI must not substitute a computed guess without flagging it.

cost_source.description: `gateway` is LiteLLM's own figure (cache discount already applied). `estimated` is a platform-side calculation and must be labelled as an estimate in the UI.
cost_source.$comment: Describes where cost_usd came from, and only that. It is deliberately not overloaded to describe the token counts, which have their own provenance in token_source: the gateway answers for the money whether or not the agent SDK produced an end-of-turn total.

token_source.description: Where input_tokens / output_tokens came from. `result` is the agent SDK's own end-of-turn total. `accumulated` is the producer summing each model response's usage as it streamed, which is what a run reports when the turn ended without a result message - a crash, an abort at the run's token ceiling, a wall-clock stop, or (measured, add-iso3166) an SDK that simply produced no result for a turn that otherwise succeeded. The two are the same quantity from different vantage points, not different quantities; `accumulated` is a floor, because a response still in flight when the stream ended is not in it. NULL means a producer predating 1.1 did not say.
token_source.$comment: Added in 1.1. Before it, usage was emitted only on the SDK's result branch, so every run that ended any other way reported no usage at all and EVAL-012's cost roll-up undercounted by exactly the abnormal runs (measured: trace $3.0879 vs gateway $3.3932 over 45 runs).

runLifecyclePayload.description: A mirror of a run state transition, so the trace timeline reads as one story.
runLifecyclePayload.$comment: NOT A SOURCE OF TRUTH (iron rule 5). The only authority on run state is the Go-owned Postgres state machine (runs.status / run_status_transitions). Never reconstruct run state by replaying these events, and never let a consumer's view of run state diverge from the runs table on the strength of this payload.
